title: Chornobyl/Chernobyl Unit 4: design features, out-of-procedure operation, and safety/regulatory framework failure
summary: Chornobyl/Chernobyl is encoded as a multi-layer severe-accident record where design, operation, prior-warning memory, and regulatory/safety framework have to be held together. INSAG-7 is used as a correction surface for earlier operator-heavy causation, not as the final word on every disputed detail.

status_history.note: Added as nuclear severe-accident / causal-status-history record.

place.location: Chornobyl/Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant Unit 4, then Soviet Union, now Ukraine

claims.claim: The IAEA topic page describes the 26 April 1986 Unit 4 accident as occurring during improper low-power testing, with loss of control leading to explosion and fire, reactor-building destruction, large radiation release, ignored safety measures, and fuel overheating through protective barriers.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: INSAG-7 is encoded because it revisits an earlier operator-action emphasis: it notes that some procedure-violation claims from 1986 were based on incorrect or incomplete information, while still treating ad hoc test changes, low-power instability, and weak safety culture as important.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: INSAG-7 also supports a design/control-system layer: the report discusses control-rod/EPS design defects, possible initial positive reactivity insertion during emergency protection actuation, low-power instrumentation/control deficiencies, and a conclusion that the RBMK control/protection system did not meet stated requirements in the relevant context.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: For the cube, Chornobyl is a causal-status-history record: it shows why accident causation must preserve later correction of the causal story itself, not merely the first official explanation.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass IAEA topic page plus INSAG-7 PDF extraction; source controversy and later scholarship deferred
limitations: Not a full Chornobyl technical/historical monograph.
Does not adjudicate all operator/design/regulatory controversies or casualty estimates.

type_payload.system: RBMK reactor / test procedure / control-protection system / Soviet nuclear safety-regulatory framework
sequence_of_events: A low-power test was conducted in an unsafe/improper operating situation.
Design/control-system characteristics and operating/test changes interacted.
Explosion and fire destroyed the reactor building and caused large radioactive release.
Later INSAG-7 correction rebalanced the causal story away from a simple operator-violation narrative.
type_payload.proximate_cause: loss of reactor control during low-power test in an unstable operating state
contributing_factors: weak safety culture and safety/regulatory framework
latent_conditions: earlier causation accounts over-weighted operator actions
safety-relevant design features were not adequately surfaced to operators and institutions
prior-warning and regulatory correction memory were inadequate
correction_surfaces: IAEA topic page and post-accident conventions
international emergency notification and assistance conventions

handling_notes: Preserve community harm and worker/family dignity; do not use nuclear accidents as spectacle.
Avoid reducing complex sociotechnical accidents to operator error or using records as blanket ideological claims about nuclear energy.

unknowns: A full source edition should include INSAG-1, INSAG-7 annexes, national investigations, and later scholarly dispute maps.
No full radiation-health, relocation, ecological, or legal consequence record is encoded.
Terminology Chornobyl/Chernobyl and Ukrainian/Russian naming conventions should be handled consistently in future revisions.
next_actions: Add a causal-status-history child record comparing INSAG-1, Soviet testimony, INSAG-7, and later scholarship.
Add Early Notification Convention and Assistance Convention as correction-memory records with legal caveats.
Add negative-control cases so MKH-PAT-0018 does not become a generic “nuclear accidents are operator/design failures” label.
